title: Auditlog pruning, replay, and error modes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the operational approach for pruning old audit events, performing controlled replay/reindex, and enumerating failure modes for the audit log storage pipeline. It focuses on making retention deterministic, enabling safe index compaction, and providing an idempotent replay/runbook for backfills and SIEM exports.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to primary audit event stream (ingest -> kafka -> enrichment -> elasticsearch index tiering -> S3 cold store).
- We assume events have stable event_id and created_at fields and the enrichment step appends an ingestion_uuid.
- This doc covers retention decisions, index lifecycle templates (hot/warm/cold/frozen), safe pruning, reindex/replay patterns, and common failure scenarios. Not a schema spec.

Retention tiers (recommended):
- Hot (0-14 days): fast nodes, full traffic routing, index refresh interval = 1s, replicas=2.
- Warm (15-90 days): less expensive SSD nodes, refresh interval = 30s, replicas=1, searchable for investigations.
- Cold (91-365 days): read-only nodes or infrequent search, index frozen copies on cheaper nodes; queries routed through async search.
- Archive (>=366 days): move to compressed S3 objects (parquet/ndjson) with partition by year/month/day; retrieval via rehydrate job that can recreate indices for reindex/replay.

Retention policy rules:
- TTL is determined by regulatory class + product sensitivity tag on event. Default global TTL = 365 days unless evidence_class = "long-retain" (e.g., legal hold, SEC) which overrides to keep until explicit release.
- Soft-delete window: when TTL expires, mark document as "pruned_pending" for 7 days to allow manual holds/appeals, then move to archive job.
- Legal hold: events tagged with legal_hold=true must be exempt from pruning; hold lifecycle managed through evidence automation (see linked playbook).

Index lifecycle and implementation notes:
- Use ILM templates per index pattern: auditlog-hot-*, auditlog-warm-*, auditlog-cold-*. ILM transitions must be based on event timestamp not ingest time.
- Rollover policy: use size+age (rollover at 50GB or 1d) to keep shard counts predictable.
- Mapping changes: never alter existing field types in place. For breaking schema changes create new index template version and migrate via replay.
- Alias strategy: maintain stable alias auditlog-search which points to latest read indices; reindex jobs update alias atomically.

Safe pruning and compaction steps:
1. Identify candidate indices using query on event_timestamp < now()-TTL and legal_hold != true and pruned_pending != true.
2. Run preflight sample query to confirm expected hit count and extract sample ids.
3. Create snapshot of affected shards into snapshot repository (weekly snapshot schedule recommended).
4. Mark indices as read-only and set pruned_pending=true at document level (7-day window).
5. After 7 days and no holds, run compaction: either delete documents and update primary store counts or move to archive S3 with compression.
6. Verify archive integrity via checksums and sample rehydrate+reindex test.

Backfill and replay playbook (idempotent):
- Goals: reindex a corrected mapping, backfill enrichment fields, or replay events into SIEM without causing duplicate downstream alerts.
- Key design: make replay idempotent using (event_id, target_system) dedupe keys. Pipeline consumers must idempotently ignore already-seen (event_id, run_id) pairs.
- Steps for a typical reindex/replay: 
  a. Create new index template (auditlog-v2-YYYYMM) with updated mappings.
  b. Launch reindex-from-source job that reads from S3 snapshots or from read-only indices. Use a cursor (byte-offset) and checkpointing.
  c. Assign run_id to this job and annotate events with replay_run_id for traceability.
  d. Consumer components (SIEM exporter, analytics) must check: if seen(event_id, target, replay_run_id) skip; else process and record seen marker in a lightweight store (redis/compact ES index).
  e. After reindex completes, swap aliases and run smoke tests (search queries, dashboard diffs).

Reindex performance and sizing notes:
- Always shard the target index so that per-shard throughput ~2-4GB/s ingest to avoid hot spots.
- Use bulk_size tuned (default 5k docs) and parallel_reindex_workers constrained by CPU and network.
- Use compression on the wire (gzip) and prefer NDJSON source batches from S3 to reduce load on restore.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: Mid-job crash during reindex -> Mitigation: job uses checkpointed slices; restart will resume from last checkpoint and use run_id to avoid duplicates.
- Failure: Replica lag / recovery stuck -> Mitigation: pause writes to target alias, reduce refresh interval, trigger shard allocation awareness check and increase replicas temporarily if node capacity available.
- Failure: Node disk watermark breach -> Mitigation: ILM move cold tier immediately; scale out storage nodes; if unavoidable, set read-only on indices and initiate emergency archive job.
- Failure: SIEM exporter duplicates alerts on replay -> Mitigation: exporter must be made idempotent (seen markers), and replays should be flagged as dry-run for first pass until markers are verified.
- Failure: Schema drift causes mapping conflicts -> Mitigation: reject inline mapping changes, create new index version; run mapping validation tool against sample payloads before reindex.

Operational runbook (quick commands):
- Mark indices read-only: curl -X PUT "/auditlog-hot-*/_settings" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"index.blocks.write": true}'
- Snapshot indices: POST /_snapshot/audit-snapshots/snap-20241101?wait_for_completion=true -d '{"indices":"auditlog-hot-*"}'
- Start controlled reindex from S3 (k8s job): kubectl create job reindex-audit-202411 --image=ghcr.io/redwood-inference/audit-reindex:stable -- env RUN_ID=20241101 SOURCE=s3://audit-archives/2023/ TARGET_ALIAS=auditlog-search
- Check active legal holds: curl GET /audit-holds/_search?q=active:true&size=1000

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Alert if unprocessed documents in hot tier > 10k (SLO: resolve within 1h).
- Alert if snapshot job fails 3 times consecutively.
- Alert on reindex job restart rate > 2x per hour.
- Track metrics: docs_pruned_per_hour, archive_throughput_MBps, reindex_throughput_docs/s, exporter_dedup_rate.

RBAC and access control considerations:
- Only staff with security-and-compliance:prune role can trigger final deletion; read-only analysts can initiate pruned_pending checks.
- Reindex and replay jobs run under service-account with least privilege: read from S3, write to specific audit indices, and write run_id metadata to audit-ops index.
- SIEM exporter requires separate credential with constrained write scope and must not be able to delete indices.

Testing checklist before any large prune/replay:
- Run mapping validation tool against 10k sample events.
- Verify run_id dedupe logic with a 2k event dry-run.
- Verify snapshot restore + reindex smoke test on staging cluster.
- Confirm legal-hold inventory is empty for targeted indices.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default global TTL for cross-region replication customers (recommend match source-customer policy; default 365).
- Implement automated reconciliation job that compares archive manifests to live index counts weekly.
- Add support for per-customer retention override stored in metadata service and surfaced to pruning job.

Appendix (useful links and references):
- Confluence: Audit Log Schema (linked above).
- Linear: SEC-412 (mapping migration) and OPS-719 (prune job run).
- GitHub: audit-pipeline PRs for idempotent replay.

Notes and history:
- Drafted after incident on 2024-08-21 where a mapping change caused 12-hour reindex outage; added shard sizing guidance and run_id dedupe.
- Will iterate after first production prune run in Q4.

Contact: Aisha Kapoor (security-and-compliance) for questions or exec sign-off.
